title: Quarterback huddle — 1:1 prep with Maya (oct)
content:
Context:
- Quick 1:1 with Maya (IC on routing + batching). Focus: unblock rollout across eu-west and discuss career/project priorities going into Q4.
- Background: last week we forced canary rollback on eu-west due to p95 spikes (observed after kernel bump). ENG-1428 tracks investigation. SRE-530 surfaced correlated infra noise.

Meeting goals (3):
1) Clear next-step plan for the eu-west rollout (who owns what by Friday).
2) Surface anything that requires me to escalate (quota, infra tickets, dodgy autoscaler).
3) Short career check-in: alignment on promotion readiness and next visible project.

Agenda (30 min, timeboxed)
- 0:00–0:03 quick sync / personal check-in (energy + blockers)
- 0:03–0:12 Tech deep dive: evidence for p95 regressions and hypothesis list (Maya)
- 0:12–0:18 Remediation plan: pairing, rollback options, monitoring thresholds (decide immediate action)
- 0:18–0:25 Resource asks / escalation required? (eng ops, Dedicated capacity change, budget)
- 0:25–0:30 Career + growth: clarify next milestone and what visible results look like

Prep notes / prompts for Maya (things to ask)
- Show the diffs from kernel bump and the changelog for the sequence-length branch. Which models hit the worst regressions?
- Have you replayed the spike with a local micro-benchmark? Results?
- Can we isolate whether KV cache pressure or batching window change caused the timing shift?
- If we throttle batch size to previous config, does p95 revert? (quick A/B test)
- Do you have a list of low-risk endpoints we can push to eu-west as a test for the fix?
- People: who needs pair debugging? Recommend pairing with Ava (SRE) and Tom (runtime kernels).

Quick metrics snapshot (bring these screenshots):
- p50/p95/p99 for eu-west over last 48h (tokens/sec, tail latency)
- error-rate trend (5xx) for last deploy window
- throughput vs concurrency chart (before/after kernel bump)
- cost-per-token delta (approx) for the variant

Immediate decisions I want by EOD Friday:
- One-line remediation committed (e.g., revert kernel change, patch batching window) or clear rollback schedule.
- Owner assigned for the interim canary gating and SLA watchdog (name + slack handle).
- Short comms draft to share with support/CS if customer-facing incidents might surface.

Escalation checklist (if we hit customer impact):
- Open SRE-530 follow-up with priority=high, tag oncall@sre, escalate to platform-eng manager.
- Request temporary Dedicated capacity bump for eu-west if autoscaler instability suspected (ops escalation: eng-ops@redwood).
- Put roll-forward/rollback play in place in Confluence (linked).

Career / coaching notes for the chat:
- Positive: Maya led the rollout plan writing and kept runbooks updated — call out specific example from last feature.
- Area: wants to own a cross-functional visible project; discuss a 60–90 day stretch: lead the eu-west stability deliverable + write a short postmortem template for perf regressions.
- Ask: Is she comfortable authoring the remediation RFC (1 pager) and leading the PR? If yes, I'll sponsor and help unblock.
- Signals for promotion readiness: consistent cross-team influence, owning an end-to-end incident remediation + measurable perf gains, mentorship of one junior.

Action items (post-meeting formatting):
- Maya: produce a 1-page hypothesis + test plan for the p95 spike (due Thu 10/14) — includes quick A/B steps and metrics to evaluate.
- Devon: follow up with eng-ops about temp capita bump and confirm who from SRE will pair (due Fri 10/15).
- Maya + Ava: pair debug session (2 hours) to run micro-benchmarks and attempt revert test (scheduled Fri afternoon).
- Devon: draft comms to CS/support if customers get noisy; keep the message conservative & include mitigations (draft due Fri EOD).
- Maya: add sequence-length distribution breakdown to the ticket ENG-1428 and link micro-benchmark logs (due Thu 10/14).

Notes to self / things to avoid saying:
- Don't promise immediate Dedicated capacity increases without ops signoff.
- Avoid technical lecture; focus on ownership and unblock.
- If Maya expresses frustration, escalate to getting her a visible win rather than more meetings.

Follow-ups / longer-term tempo (post-stability):
- 30-day plan: identify 2 perf knobs that consistently lower p95 across models (pick one to Q4 spike-proof).
- Pair Maya with Tom on kernel selection heuristics (shadowing + code review).
- Add a short-runbook template for rollout gating (I will own the PR to the playbook).

Random scratchpad lines (useful soundbites):
- "Ship small, measure large" — remind about incremental gating.
- "If it's noisy at 99, focus on queueing/serialization first."
- Ask: "Which part feels like an engineering problem vs platform config?"

Prep checklist for the meeting (bring these):
- Local benchmark output (tar.gz or link) or screenshots attached.
- Links to ENG-1428 and SRE-530.
- Timeline of deploys in the last 72 hours.
- One proposed short comms paragraph (for CS) — I will edit live.

End-of-doc: quick personal note — Maya's been balancing too many contexts; prioritize removing one recurring meeting (recommend: weekly infra sync) so she can focus on stability.

-- Devon (notes)
